$comment: What the agent sandbox images (Dockerfile) install: everything here goes into all three images (standard, full, engineering), "office" only into the full one and "engineering" only into the engineering one. Source for SANDBOX_IMAGE_TOOLS / SANDBOX_NODE_PACKAGES / SANDBOX_PYTHON_PACKAGES in supabase/functions/_shared/ai-workforce/sandbox.ts (tests/unit/ai-workforce/sandboxImage.test.ts keeps them in step) and for the Clateway Claude Code plugin's scanner. Node packages are global (NODE_PATH) and linked into /workspace/node_modules at sandbox start, so they work without network.

office.$comment: Only in the full image (Dockerfile build argument IMAGE_VARIANT=full, runtime clateway_workspace_full): LibreOffice headless adds ~500 MB, so the standard image stays small and starts faster.

programs.$comment: Programs a package may run as they are (phase 4 of docs/BUILD_PLANS/claude-agent-import.md): Claude Code and the Agent SDK. Their versions are the ones under npm / pip below; the build arguments CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION / CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION pin an exact version over them for a release. They reach models only through the Clateway gateway (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, set per sandbox) and MCP servers only through the managed files in /etc/claude-code.

engineering.$comment: Only in the engineering image (Dockerfile build argument IMAGE_VARIANT=engineering, runtime clateway_workspace_eng), for agents that design machines: parametric CAD with CadQuery and build123d on one OpenCascade (cadquery-ocp-novtk 7.9: build123d 0.12 and CadQuery 2.8 both run on it; CadQuery is installed without its viewer dependencies, see pip_no_deps), meshes and glTF / GLB export, FEA with CalculiX, discrete-event throughput with SimPy, plant models as FMUs (FMPy runs them, PythonFMU builds them), IEC 61131-3 PLC software with OpenPLC v3 (matiec iec2c compiler, runtime and its web editor), OPC UA with asyncua, and CycloneDX SBOMs. All of it works without internet.

pip_no_deps.$comment: CadQuery 2.8 without its declared dependencies on VTK, casadi and trame (its viewer, the constraint solver and the notebook widgets): with them it would bring a second OpenCascade with VTK (about 250 MB) that breaks build123d and does not fit the image. clateway_cq_shim.py (engineering/) lets CadQuery load without VTK and casadi and refuses their use with a plain error; modelling and STEP, STL, glTF and DXF export work. Checked by running the SCM-600 R2 CadQuery model: the same 84 parts, masses and EBOM byte for byte, and the same meshes (face counts, volumes, bounds).

constraints.$comment: Versions of packages the standard part already has that this part must move: build123d's materials (threejs-materials) need pillow 12.2, moviepy pins pillow < 12 only as a precaution (its clips and GIFs were checked on 12.2 in this image).

openplc.$comment: OpenPLC v3 (github.com/thiagoralves/OpenPLC_v3, GPL-3.0) at a pinned commit, installed with its own installer (target docker) into /opt/openplc, root-owned. The openplc command copies its webserver folder into /workspace/openplc on first use and runs it as the sandbox user: the web editor on ui_port, Modbus TCP on modbus_port (not 502, which needs root). openplc-ui puts the editor behind a preview link (it keeps the login itself and rewrites the editor's root links), opcua-bridge publishes the PLC's located variables as an OPC UA server.

pythonfmu_export.$comment: PythonFMU ships its FMU library (libpythonfmu-export.so) for x86 Linux only; the image compiles it from this source for ARM64, the commit of the pythonfmu release above (tag v0.7.0).

leave_out.$comment: What the engineering image leaves out of the standard set, to stay under AgentCore's 2,048 MB image limit: VS Code in the browser (code-server; OpenPLC brings its own editor), the Semgrep scanner and its rules, the Trivy database (the trivy command stays and needs a network for it), and the VS Code extension tooling.

editor.$comment: VS Code in the browser (code-server, standalone release with its own Node), in both images. Pinned and checked against the SHA-256 of the release tarballs. Started only by the workspace server (op start_editor) for the person a task acts for, bound to 127.0.0.1, no extensions, no marketplace, no telemetry; reached through the preview proxy (ai-workforce-preview /e/<token>/).
